newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up 0.34 pct in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up 0.34 pct in volatile trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended up 0.34 percent in seesaw trade ahead of Monday's options settlements, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares rose 227 points to 66,802 points at the close.
Volume was a high 581.1 million reais ($559.1 million), of which 3.82 million reais were due to options which were exercised.

Analysts said details of the telecommunications bill which was sent to Congress Thursday were generally welcomed but they noted the effects of the planned changes in the sector will only be factored in share prices after the settlement.
Preferred stocks of Telebras closed up 1.25 percent to 77.05 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, fell 1.47 percent to 1,818 points.

BCN preferred stock closed at 10.50 reais, off 0.9 percent, after one-day suspension. Trade resumed after the bank confirmed it was holding talks to sell a controlling stake to Banco BBA Creditanstalt but denied it had already sold such a stake to the bank as some newspapers reported.
